title: ServiceStatus
description: One service, as semiont status reads it: where it runs, its state, and whether it answers. Nothing is reported that the launcher did not observe: an endpoint is named only when the stack's record or the descriptor names one, and a page to open only when the service answers.

role.description: The service, as semiont status names it.

product.description: The product its driver names (Neo4j, Keycloak), when its record names a driver.

runsOn.description: Where it runs: the runtime its container runs under, external (somebody else runs it), or host (a process on this machine). Absent when nothing runs it.

state.description: running: its container runs. stopped: its container exists and does not run (containerState says how). reachable, unreachable: somebody else runs it, and its endpoint answers or does not. absent: there is no container of it. not-configured: the stack's documents ask for none.

containerState.description: The runtime's own word for a container that is not running (exited, created).

counted.description: Whether its health counts toward its knowledge base's: a service the documents ask for none of, and a telemetry backend --no-observe leaves out, do not.

probe.description: The endpoint the launcher asks its health of: an http URL, or tcp://host:port.

page.description: The page a person opens: the Browser, Jaeger's and Prometheus's interfaces, the collector's metrics readout. Present only when the service answers. The collector's OTLP receiver is never one.

realm.description: For the issuer the knowledge base signs in at, when it is the machine's: its realm there.

serves.description: For a service several knowledge bases share: the name of each it serves, as knowledgeBases names them.
